text.p: The following are some of the leading stories in Finnish papers this morning.
HELSINGIN SANOMAT

- European Commission is demanding Finland to withdraw its tax exemption on birch sweetener xylitol, not accepting Finnish research that it promotes national health by preventing tooth caries. Finnish experts baffled.
- The number of Finns opposing EMU increase their lead over those in favour of joining monetary union, now at 46 percent against 36 percent with 17 percent undecided, Taloustutkimus survey shows.
- Central Union of Trade and Commerce recommends hardware stores to lock up spray paints to keep them out of reach for graffiti-painting youngsters.
- Finland experiences 10 earthquakes a year on average but the only damage caused in general are pelargonia falling from window ledges or mixed well water, seismologist says.
- Government planning to make permanent some 3,500 jobs currently in employment schemes, finance ministry says.

- The shift towards information society has increased unemployment in Finland, with computerisation cutting more jobs than growth in the information technology sector has compensated, Etlatieto managing director Pekka Yla-Anttila says.
- Only a third of the young living in Helsinki's concrete suburbs voted in last autumn's local polls, study shows.

- Mobile phone retailer Makitorppa found lively demand for an April Fool's mobile phone model advertised to make possible the use of internet in most television sets, and to have a built in remote control also for video recorders, CD players and radios. Nokia R&D director says such a handset would be technically possible.

- State investment fund Suomen Teollisuussijoitus which is to re-invest proceeds from privatisation made 115 million markka worth of equity investment last year, 75 million into other venture capital funds.
KAUPPALEHTI
- Finnish small and medium sized companies are more international than their European counterparts, but still need help in marketing, study made in five countries shows.
- Merita says is expanding in project finance.
- State asset management company Arsenal says sells 400,000 Orion A shares.
- Normal copyright legislation suits the internet or can easily be adapted to it, lawyer says.
AAMULEHTI
- Helsinki authorities to start changing used syringes for new ones on Friday in an attempt to reduce the risk of infection among drug abusers.
- Gerhard von Wendt proposed to become non-executive chairman of Outokumpu's board.
TURUN SANOMAT
- Arto Alkkiomaki, the leader of a group of cooperative banks opposing tighter cooperation around OKOBANK, says some 60-70 banks are in his group, which may be enough to prevent the cooperation plan.
- Pouching is becoming professional and organised in southern Finland, hunter says.
- Turku Telephone operator Turun Puhelin which the city plans to sell posted 35 million markka profit on net sales of 276 million in 1996.
HUFVUDSTADSBLADET
- Finnish and Swedish officials meeting NATO officials in Brussels marked that the countries have a right to change their current non-aligned security policy, sources say.

- World press gave Finland little attention in coverage of the U.S.-Russian summit on March 21, but the capital name Helsinki was much printed, albeit with a few spelling mistakes such as Helsinski and Helsinky.
